title: What Happened Before the Stop: A Fixed-Size Black Box With a Hash Chain, Wrap-Around That Can Still Be Verified, and What Tampering Leaves Behind

questions.question: Why must recording to the black box never block, allocate or fail in the control loop?
options: A recorder that can stall the loop is a hazard of its own
The black box has only a few kilobytes of memory
A blocking write would put the events out of order
The chain value takes too long to compute
questions.explanation: The recorder runs inside the loop that keeps the robot safe. If writing a record could stall or throw, the recorder would be one more thing that can stop that loop.

questions.question: The ring has wrapped. A check that starts the chain at zero says what about the first event left?
options: Fine: the first event left is the start of a new chain
Missing: a gap at the first event left
Altered: it has lost its predecessor
Nothing: the chain is not checked after a wrap
questions.explanation: The box keeps the chain value of the last event overwritten and verify starts from it. The first event left was chained to one that has been overwritten. Keeping that one's chain value lets the check start from the right place: 12 dropped, verified from the kept link.

questions.question: An event is deleted from the middle of the log. What does verify report?
options: altered, at the event after the one deleted
gap: something is missing, and it is reported before the chain mismatch that the deletion also causes
Nothing: the chain closes up over a deletion
A time going back
questions.explanation: A deletion breaks the sequence and the chain. The sequence is checked first, because a missing event is the more useful thing to be told.

questions.question: The last five events are cut off. What does verify say, and what would catch it?
options: A gap at the first missing event
It does not: the end of a chain has nothing after it to disagree, and it needs the latest chain value kept somewhere else
Altered, at the last event left
It finds it, from the count of events dropped
questions.explanation: Every event vouches for the ones before it. The newest have nothing after them, so cutting them off leaves a chain that still checks.

questions.question: The six events before the stop showed the range falling with the speed at 1.50 throughout. What does that tell you?
options: The range sensor had failed and was reading low
The wall was moving toward the robot at 1.5 m/s
The speed was being limited by the fence
The robot did not slow for the wall at all, which the stop event with its cause bits alone would not have shown
questions.explanation: The range fell by 0.15 m a tick while the speed stayed at 1.50 m/s. The stop event says that it stopped; the window before it says it never slowed.

questions.question: Why order events by sequence number and not by the clock?
options: A sequence number is shorter to store than a time
The clock is too coarse to separate two events in one tick
The clock is not available inside the control loop
The clock can be set back, and times 5, 4, 6 were kept in order by sequence and counted as one time going back
questions.explanation: The box counts its own events, and nothing can set that count back. A clock that was adjusted would otherwise reorder the record.
